definition: Teleology is a way of understanding behavior as purposeful and shaped by a person’s goals and psychological motives, rather than as a purely passive response to outside influences. In this Adlerian sense, it highlights people as active agents whose choices are guided by aims such as belonging, control, self-consistency, superiority, goal pursuit, and avoiding failure or negative feelings.

reasons: The packet never provides a standalone definition of teleology; it only mentions that the study “introduces Adler’s teleology” to examine motivations behind users’ proactive behavior.

The definition’s claim that teleology is “a way of understanding behavior as purposeful” and “rather than as a purely passive response” is not stated explicitly in the packet (it is only indirectly suggested by contrasting passive recipients with proactive agents).

While the listed motivational aims (belonging, control/security, self-consistency, superiority, goal orientation, avoidance of failure/negative emotions) are present in the packet as the study’s six dimensions, the packet does not justify extending them into an “Adlerian sense” definition of teleology beyond that specific use.
